note: Government round 3 (part B): Nigerian political history and external relations - pre-colonial systems, colonial administration, nationalism, constitutional development, First to Fourth Republics, military rule, Nigerian federalism, foreign policy, relations with other countries and international organisations, with a heads-of-government table and an international-bodies table as data passages.

passages.title: Nigeria's heads of government, 1960 to 1999
passages.text:
The table shows Nigeria's heads of
government from independence to 1999 and
the route by which each came to power. PM
means Prime Minister; 'succession' means
that the leader took over after the death
of the previous head of state.

Leader             Years     Route
Balewa (PM)        1960-66   election
Aguiyi-Ironsi      1966      coup
Gowon              1966-75   coup
Murtala Mohammed   1975-76   coup
Obasanjo           1976-79   succession
Shagari            1979-83   election
Buhari             1983-85   coup
Babangida          1985-93   coup
Shonekan           1993      appointment
Abacha             1993-98   coup
Abubakar           1998-99   succession

passages.title: Some international bodies to which Nigeria belongs
passages.text:
The table shows five international bodies
to which Nigeria belongs, the year each
was founded and the city where its
headquarters is located. Nigeria joined
the two oldest bodies in the year of its
independence, was a founding member of the
two bodies founded in 1963 and 1975, and
joined the body founded in 1960 in 1971.

Body          Founded  Headquarters
Commonwealth  1931     London
UN            1945     New York
OPEC          1960     Vienna
OAU           1963     Addis Ababa
ECOWAS        1975     Abuja

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the number of leaders who came to power through a military coup is
questions.explanation: Aguiyi-Ironsi, Gowon, Murtala Mohammed, Buhari, Babangida and Abacha are all shown as coming to power by coup.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the elected civilian governments overthrown by the military were those of
questions.A: Shagari and Shonekan
questions.B: Balewa and Shonekan
questions.C: Balewa and Shagari
questions.D: Obasanjo and Abubakar
questions.explanation: Only Balewa (1960) and Shagari (1979) came to power by election, and each was removed by a coup; Shonekan was appointed, not elected.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the military head of state with the longest continuous period in office was
questions.A: Obasanjo
questions.B: Babangida
questions.C: Abacha
questions.D: Gowon
questions.explanation: Gowon ruled from 1966 to 1975, about nine years; Babangida ruled for eight.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the two leaders who came to power by succession are alike in that each
questions.A: was removed from office by a military coup
questions.B: later handed over power to an elected civilian government
questions.C: was elected President of Nigeria after leaving the army
questions.D: ruled Nigeria for more than five years
questions.explanation: Obasanjo handed over to Shagari in 1979 and Abubakar handed over to Obasanjo in 1999.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the leader shown as coming to power by appointment headed
questions.A: the first elected civilian government of the Second Republic under the 1979 Constitution
questions.B: the Supreme Military Council that directed the federal side during the civil war
questions.C: the Interim National Government formed after the annulment of the June 12, 1993 election
questions.D: the Constituent Assembly that debated and approved the draft of the 1979 Constitution
questions.explanation: Chief Ernest Shonekan was appointed by Babangida to head the Interim National Government in August 1993.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The period 1979 to 1983 in the table above corresponds to
questions.A: the Fourth Republic
questions.B: the First Republic
questions.C: the Third Republic
questions.D: the Second Republic
questions.explanation: Shagari's elected government of 1979 to 1983 was Nigeria's Second Republic.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The leader in the table above whose removal in 1975 took place while he was attending an OAU summit abroad was
questions.A: Murtala Mohammed
questions.B: Gowon
questions.C: Aguiyi-Ironsi
questions.D: Balewa
questions.explanation: Gowon was overthrown on 29 July 1975 while attending the OAU summit in Kampala, Uganda.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Judging from the table above, of the thirty-nine years between October 1960 and May 1999, roughly how many were spent under military rule?
questions.A: about 19 years
questions.B: about 10 years
questions.C: about 29 years
questions.D: about 35 years
questions.explanation: January 1966 to October 1979 (about 13.75 years), December 1983 to August 1993 (about 9.7 years) and November 1993 to May 1999 (about 5.5 years) add up to roughly 29 years.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the body whose headquarters is in a Nigerian city is
questions.A: the Commonwealth
questions.B: OAU
questions.C: OPEC
questions.D: ECOWAS
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission, Parliament and Court of Justice are all located in Abuja.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: From the table above, the oldest of the five bodies is
questions.A: the UN
questions.B: the Commonwealth
questions.C: OPEC
questions.D: the OAU
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth dates from the Statute of Westminster of 1931; the UN was founded in 1945.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria was suspended from one of the bodies in the table above in 1995 after the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists. That body was
questions.A: OPEC
questions.B: the UN
questions.C: the Commonwealth
questions.D: ECOWAS
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth suspended Nigeria at its Auckland meeting in November 1995 and readmitted it in May 1999.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria joined the body in the table above with its headquarters in Vienna in 1971 mainly because
questions.A: it wished to promote free trade with Austria
questions.B: it wanted to attract European tourists to Nigeria
questions.C: it needed loans to rebuild after the civil war
questions.D: it had become a major exporter of crude oil by that time
questions.explanation: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries; Nigeria's oil output rose sharply after the civil war.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The body in the table above founded in 1963 no longer exists under that name because
questions.A: its members withdrew to join ECOWAS
questions.B: it was replaced by the African Union in 2002
questions.C: it was dissolved by the UN Security Council
questions.D: it merged with the Commonwealth in 1995
questions.explanation: The OAU was replaced by the African Union at Durban in July 2002.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: According to the passage above, Nigeria was a founding member of
questions.A: OPEC and the OAU
questions.B: the UN and the Commonwealth
questions.C: the OAU and ECOWAS
questions.D: the UN and OPEC
questions.explanation: Nigeria signed the OAU Charter in 1963 and the ECOWAS Treaty of Lagos in 1975; it joined the UN and Commonwealth in 1960 and OPEC in 1971.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The most powerful organ of the body in the table above headquartered in New York is the
questions.A: Economic and Social Council
questions.B: General Assembly
questions.C: Trusteeship Council
questions.D: Security Council
questions.explanation: The UN Security Council can pass binding resolutions and authorise sanctions and the use of force.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa/Fulani emirates, the official who served as the Emir's chief adviser and head of administration, comparable to a prime minister, was the
questions.A: Madawaki
questions.B: Waziri
questions.C: Sarkin Fada
questions.D: Dogari
questions.explanation: The Waziri headed the emirate's administration; the Madawaki commanded the army, the Sarkin Fada headed the palace staff and the Dogari were the bodyguards.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the Oyo Empire, an Alaafin who was presented with an empty calabash or parrot's eggs by the Oyo Mesi was expected to
questions.A: lead the army in person against the Dahomeans
questions.B: appoint a new Bashorun to head the council
questions.C: commit suicide because his people had rejected him
questions.D: hand over the throne to the Aremo immediately
questions.explanation: The empty calabash symbolised rejection; the Alaafin was required to take his own life, a check on royal tyranny.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The pre-colonial Igbo political system is described as acephalous because
questions.A: all decisions were taken by a council appointed by a neighbouring empire
questions.B: every village was ruled by a powerful king with a standing army
questions.C: the people were governed by priests who ruled in the name of the gods
questions.D: there was no paramount ruler and authority was shared among elders, age grades and title holders
questions.explanation: Acephalous means headless; Igbo villages governed themselves through assemblies and lineage heads rather than kings.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following checked the powers of the Alaafin of Oyo?
questions.A: the Ilari messengers he appointed
questions.B: the Oyo Mesi and the Ogboni cult
questions.C: the Ajele who collected tribute for him
questions.D: the Baale of the outlying villages
questions.explanation: The Oyo Mesi could reject an Alaafin, and the Ogboni cult mediated between the Alaafin and the Oyo Mesi; the Ilari and Ajele were his own agents.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The commander of the Oyo army who lived outside the capital and was expected to win every battle or commit suicide was the
questions.A: Aremo
questions.B: Bashorun
questions.C: Are-Ona-Kakanfo
questions.D: Ooni
questions.explanation: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo led the army from a provincial town; defeat brought disgrace and death.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In pre-colonial Igbo society, public works such as clearing paths and guarding the village were carried out mainly by
questions.A: the oracle priests
questions.B: the Ofo title holders
questions.C: the Umuada
questions.D: the age grades
questions.explanation: Age grades of young men performed communal labour and security duties; the elders and Ofo holders took decisions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Indirect rule worked most smoothly in Northern Nigeria mainly because
questions.A: the British sent far more officers to the North than to the South
questions.B: the emirate system was already centralised, with established taxation and courts
questions.C: the emirs were educated in English and understood colonial law
questions.D: the Northern peoples had no rulers of their own before 1900
questions.explanation: Lugard simply ruled through the existing emirs, their treasuries and their Islamic courts.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The introduction of warrant chiefs in Igboland by the British failed largely because
questions.A: the Igbo already had emirs who resented the new appointments
questions.B: the warrant chiefs refused to collect taxes for the colonial government
questions.C: the Igbo had no tradition of chiefs with such powers, so the warrant chiefs were seen as imposed strangers
questions.D: the British paid the warrant chiefs too little to make the office attractive
questions.explanation: Warrant chiefs abused powers the Igbo had never given to any single man, provoking the Aba Women's Riot of 1929.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the Sokoto Caliphate, legal cases were decided according to Islamic law by the
questions.A: Sarkin Ruwa
questions.B: Galadima
questions.C: Hakimi
questions.D: Alkali
questions.explanation: The Alkali presided over the Sharia courts; the Galadima administered the capital, the Hakimi a district and the Sarkin Ruwa fishing and rivers.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Emir's officer in charge of a district, who collected taxes and kept order there on his behalf, was the
questions.A: Dagaci
questions.B: Hakimi
questions.C: Waziri
questions.D: Ma'aji
questions.explanation: District heads (Hakimai) supervised village heads (Dagatai); the Ma'aji was the treasurer.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Decisions in a pre-colonial Igbo village were taken at a general assembly where every adult male could speak and the elders announced the consensus. This shows that Igbo government was
questions.A: theocratic and centralised
questions.B: monarchical and hereditary
questions.C: participatory and democratic
questions.D: military and authoritarian
questions.explanation: The village assembly (ama-ala) practised a form of direct democracy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The cattle tax collected in the pre-colonial emirates of Northern Nigeria was known as
questions.A: Jizya
questions.B: Zakat
questions.C: Kharaj
questions.D: Jangali
questions.explanation: Jangali was levied on Fulani herdsmen's cattle; Zakat was the religious alms tax, Kharaj the land tax and Jizya the tax on non-Muslims.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the Benin kingdom, the Uzama n'Ihinron were
questions.A: the palace chiefs who ran the Oba's household
questions.B: the hereditary kingmakers who installed the Oba
questions.C: the town chiefs who collected tribute from villages
questions.D: the war commanders who led the army in battle
questions.explanation: The seven Uzama were the senior hereditary nobles of Benin with the right to crown the Oba.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The British created the office of Tor Tiv in 1947 because
questions.A: the previous Tor Tiv had died without a successor
questions.B: the Tiv demanded a king to match the emirs of the far North
questions.C: the Tiv had no paramount ruler through whom indirect rule could operate
questions.D: the Tiv had been conquered by the Sokoto Caliphate
questions.explanation: Like the Igbo, the Tiv had a segmentary system, so the colonial government invented a paramount chief.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Berlin Conference of 1884 to 1885 is important in the history of Nigeria because it
questions.A: created the Royal Niger Company and granted it a monopoly of trade along the whole course of the Niger
questions.B: abolished the trans-Atlantic slave trade and established the Colony of Lagos as a British possession
questions.C: granted Nigeria internal self-government under British protection as a first step towards independence
questions.D: laid down the rules by which European powers partitioned Africa and recognised British claims to the Niger area
questions.explanation: The conference's principle of effective occupation triggered the scramble in which Britain secured the Niger basin.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The British government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company in 1899 mainly because
questions.A: the company had become too profitable and refused to pay any part of its large earnings to the British Treasury
questions.B: it wanted to administer the territory directly in order to check French expansion and end the company's trade monopoly
questions.C: African rulers had signed new treaties with the company that the British government refused to recognise as valid
questions.D: the company had asked to be relieved of its charter after making heavy losses in the trade with the interior
questions.explanation: From 1 January 1900 the Crown took over the company's territories as the Protectorates of Northern and Southern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Lagos became a British colony in 1861 through
questions.A: the purchase of the island from the Portuguese traders who owned it
questions.B: a plebiscite in which the people of Lagos voted for British rule
questions.C: a treaty of cession signed by Oba Dosunmu under the threat of naval bombardment
questions.D: a decision of the Berlin Conference of European powers
questions.explanation: Consul Beecroft's successors forced Dosunmu (Docemo) to cede Lagos, ostensibly to stop the slave trade.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The three pillars of indirect rule in Nigeria were the
questions.A: chartered company, missionaries and traders
questions.B: governor, legislative council and executive council
questions.C: district officer, resident and high commissioner
questions.D: native authority, native treasury and native courts
questions.explanation: Traditional rulers governed as native authorities, financed by native treasuries, and administered justice through native courts.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Adubi War of 1918 in Egbaland was a protest against
questions.A: the abolition of the slave trade by the British navy
questions.B: the introduction of direct taxation and forced labour under colonial rule
questions.C: the building of the railway through Abeokuta
questions.D: the appointment of an Alake by the colonial government
questions.explanation: Direct taxation was extended to the West in 1918, provoking the Egba rising in which many people died.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 was sparked by
questions.A: the closure of the local markets by the Royal Niger Company in retaliation for the boycott of its goods
questions.B: the arrest and detention of Herbert Macaulay by the colonial police for his criticism of the government
questions.C: rumours that women would be taxed following a count of persons and property ordered by warrant chiefs
questions.D: the introduction of a new colonial currency that traders in the Eastern markets refused to accept
questions.explanation: Women in Oloko and other towns attacked warrant chiefs and native courts; the riot led to reforms of administration in the East.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major difference between British indirect rule and French assimilation was that
questions.A: the French preserved African customs while the British abolished them
questions.B: the British gave Africans seats in the Westminster parliament while the French did not
questions.C: the French used chartered companies while the British used colonial officers
questions.D: the British governed through traditional rulers while the French aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen through direct rule
questions.explanation: Assimilation treated colonies as overseas parts of France; indirect rule kept African institutions under British supervision.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under French colonial policy, the few Africans who acquired French citizenship by meeting educational and cultural conditions were called
questions.A: indigènes
questions.B: évolués
questions.C: commandants
questions.D: assimilators
questions.explanation: Évolués enjoyed the rights of citizens; the mass of subjects (indigènes) were governed under the harsh indigénat code.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Lord Lugard's main economic argument for joining the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914 was that
questions.A: a single territory would be easier for the Royal Niger Company to trade in
questions.B: the North had rich oil deposits that the South could market
questions.C: the customs revenue of the South could cover the deficit of the North and end the imperial grant
questions.D: the South needed the North's cotton to feed its textile mills
questions.explanation: The North depended on grants from Britain and Southern Nigeria; amalgamation made the whole territory self-financing.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Colonial railways in Nigeria were built from the coast into the interior mainly in order to
questions.A: provide employment for demobilised soldiers
questions.B: enable Nigerians to travel freely between the regions
questions.C: link Nigeria with the French colonies to the north
questions.D: carry export crops and minerals cheaply to the ports
questions.explanation: Lines from Lagos and Port Harcourt reached Kano and the Jos tin fields to move groundnuts, cotton and tin for export.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Council set up by Lugard in 1914 was ineffective mainly because
questions.A: it met in London where Nigerian members could not travel
questions.B: it was purely advisory and dominated by officials, and its nominated Nigerian members rarely attended
questions.C: it was made up entirely of elected Nigerians who opposed the governor
questions.D: it had powers to make laws that the governor refused to sign
questions.explanation: The Council could only discuss matters put before it; it was replaced by the Legislative Council of 1922.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Indirect rule was only partially successful in Yorubaland mainly because
questions.A: the British refused to recognise the Alaafin of Oyo or any other Oba as a ruler and appointed their own officials instead
questions.B: the Yoruba had never had kings or chiefs of any kind before the arrival of the British and rejected the idea of rulers
questions.C: the powers of the Obas were traditionally limited by councils, so making them sole native authorities distorted the system
questions.D: the Yoruba paid no taxes of any kind to their traditional rulers and so refused to pay the new colonial taxes as well
questions.explanation: Obas given unchecked colonial backing became unpopular, as the Egba protests against the Alake in 1948 showed.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The marketing boards created by the colonial government from 1947 were meant to stabilise producer prices, but in practice they
questions.A: abolished the export of cocoa and groundnuts
questions.B: paid farmers more than world prices and ran into heavy debt
questions.C: handed all their profits to the farmers' cooperatives
questions.D: paid farmers less than world prices and built up large surpluses for government use
questions.explanation: The boards' surpluses later financed regional development under the 1954 constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Christian missionaries aided imperial penetration of Nigeria mainly by
questions.A: raising and equipping private armies that conquered the coastal kingdoms on behalf of the British Crown
questions.B: establishing schools and churches that spread European values and by appealing for British protection
questions.C: buying up land from the chiefs along the coast and handing it over to the British Crown as colonies
questions.D: organising the export of palm oil to Liverpool and financing the trading companies with church funds
questions.explanation: Missionary activity from the 1840s created converts sympathetic to European rule and drew the British into local disputes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Oil Rivers Protectorate declared in 1885 was renamed the Niger Coast Protectorate in 1893 and in 1900 became part of the
questions.A: Protectorate of Northern Nigeria
questions.B: Colony of Lagos
questions.C: Protectorate of Southern Nigeria
questions.D: Royal Niger Company territories
questions.explanation: In 1900 the Niger Coast Protectorate and the company's southern territories were merged as the Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Herbert Macaulay founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party in 1923 primarily to
questions.A: demand the immediate independence of Nigeria from Britain
questions.B: organise a general strike of railway workers in Lagos
questions.C: campaign for the amalgamation of Nigeria with the Gold Coast
questions.D: contest the Lagos seats created by the elective principle of the Clifford Constitution
questions.explanation: The NNDP won all three Lagos seats in the 1923, 1928 and 1933 elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The National Congress of British West Africa, formed in 1920 under Casely Hayford, is credited with
questions.A: leading the armed struggle for independence in the Gold Coast
questions.B: pressing for elective representation, which the Clifford Constitution granted in 1922
questions.C: founding the first university in West Africa at Ibadan
questions.D: negotiating the independence of Nigeria in 1960
questions.explanation: Though Governor Clifford ridiculed the Congress, his 1922 constitution conceded four elected seats.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Youth Movement declined after 1941 because of
questions.A: its decision to merge with the Northern People's Congress, which most of its Lagos members refused to accept
questions.B: the death of its founder Herbert Macaulay in that year and the failure of the members to agree on a successor to him
questions.C: a leadership quarrel over whether Ikoli or Akinsanya should fill a Legislative Council seat, which split it along ethnic lines
questions.D: the colonial government's ban on all political meetings during the Second World War, which stopped its activities
questions.explanation: Azikiwe and his supporters left the NYM after the crisis, which many saw as the beginning of ethnic politics in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The West African Pilot, founded by Nnamdi Azikiwe in 1937, advanced nationalism by
questions.A: serving as the newspaper of the Northern emirates
questions.B: publishing the official policies of the colonial government
questions.C: printing only news from Britain and the Gold Coast
questions.D: exposing colonial injustices and spreading nationalist ideas to a mass readership
questions.explanation: Azikiwe's chain of newspapers gave nationalists a platform and trained a generation of journalists.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Zikist Movement formed in 1946 differed from earlier nationalist bodies in that it
questions.A: was made up entirely of traditional rulers
questions.B: advocated militant, revolutionary methods against colonial rule
questions.C: supported the Richards Constitution of 1946
questions.D: sought independence for the Northern Region only
questions.explanation: Zikists called for positive action and civil disobedience; the movement was banned in 1950.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The general strike of 1945 led by Michael Imoudu and the shooting of coal miners at Enugu in 1949 contributed to nationalism by
questions.A: ending the influence of the trade unions in Nigerian politics and leaving the field to the political parties
questions.B: persuading the colonial government to grant independence immediately without any further constitutional talks
questions.C: uniting workers and politicians against colonial rule and winning wide sympathy for the nationalist cause
questions.D: leading directly to the formation of the Northern People's Congress as a party of workers and miners
questions.explanation: The Iva Valley shooting, in which 21 miners died, led nationalists to form the National Emergency Committee.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Atlantic Charter of 1941 encouraged African nationalists because
questions.A: it gave African soldiers the right to vote in British elections
questions.B: it promised that Britain would withdraw from Africa within five years
questions.C: it created the United Nations Trusteeship Council
questions.D: it affirmed the right of all peoples to choose the form of government under which they live
questions.explanation: Churchill later said the Charter applied only to Europe, but nationalists insisted it applied to the colonies too.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigerian ex-servicemen who returned from the Second World War strengthened nationalist agitation because they
questions.A: were given seats in the Legislative Council by the colonial government and used them to demand independence
questions.B: had fought alongside Europeans, lost their awe of the white man and resented being denied the rewards promised to them
questions.C: brought back large sums of money from the war which they used to finance the political parties and newspapers
questions.D: had been trained in Britain as colonial administrators and returned to take over the senior posts in the service
questions.explanation: Ex-servicemen swelled the ranks of the nationalist movements in Nigeria and the Gold Coast.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Anthony Enahoro's motion in the House of Representatives in March 1953 called for
questions.A: the removal of the Governor-General
questions.B: the creation of the Mid-West Region
questions.C: self-government for Nigeria in 1956
questions.D: a boycott of the 1954 federal election
questions.explanation: Northern members proposed 'as soon as practicable' instead of 1956, and the resulting crisis led to the 1953 London conference.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Kano riots of May 1953 followed
questions.A: the decision of the colonial government to move the federal capital from Lagos to Kaduna against Southern wishes
questions.B: the announcement of the results of the 1953 census, which showed that the North had lost its population majority
questions.C: the arrest of Aminu Kano by the Native Authority police for organising a strike of workers in the groundnut trade
questions.D: the jeering of Northern legislators in Lagos over the self-government motion and an Action Group campaign tour of Kano
questions.explanation: Northern anger at being jeered in Lagos exploded when the AG delegation arrived in Kano; scores of people died.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The NCNC delegation that travelled to London in 1947 went to
questions.A: ask Britain to build more railways in Nigeria
questions.B: protest against the Richards Constitution and demand its review
questions.C: negotiate the end of the Second World War
questions.D: request the appointment of Azikiwe as Governor
questions.explanation: The Colonial Secretary told the delegation to go home and work the constitution, but the protest hastened its review.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Pan-African Congress held in Manchester in 1945 was significant because it
questions.A: founded the Organisation of African Unity and chose Addis Ababa as the headquarters of the new body
questions.B: was the first meeting of African heads of state after independence and adopted a charter for the continent
questions.C: demanded independence for African colonies and brought together future leaders such as Nkrumah and Kenyatta
questions.D: decided to partition Africa among the European powers and laid down rules for the effective occupation of colonies
questions.explanation: The Manchester Congress marked the shift of Pan-Africanism from protest to a demand for self-government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The West African Students' Union, founded in London in 1925 by Ladipo Solanke,
questions.A: campaigned for West Africans to settle permanently in Britain
questions.B: was a sports club for West African students at Oxford
questions.C: was created by the Colonial Office to recruit civil servants
questions.D: served as a training ground for nationalists and a pressure group against colonial policies
questions.explanation: WASU hosted and influenced many future leaders, including Awolowo and Nkrumah.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Egba women's protests of 1947 to 1948 led by Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti were directed against
questions.A: the closure of girls' schools in Abeokuta
questions.B: the taxation of women and the abuses of the Alake's native authority
questions.C: the recruitment of women into the colonial army
questions.D: the ban on women trading in the Lagos markets
questions.explanation: The Abeokuta Women's Union forced the Alake, Oba Ademola II, to go into temporary exile in 1949.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following was an internal factor in the growth of Nigerian nationalism?
questions.A: the independence of India and Pakistan in 1947
questions.B: the signing of the Atlantic Charter in 1941
questions.C: discrimination against educated Africans in the colonial civil service
questions.D: the victory of the Labour Party in Britain in 1945
questions.explanation: Educated Nigerians denied senior posts and equal pay turned to politics; the other options are external factors.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Ghana's independence in March 1957 affected Nigerian nationalism by
questions.A: ending the influence of Pan-Africanism in Nigeria
questions.B: persuading Nigerian leaders to postpone independence indefinitely
questions.C: leading Nigeria to join Ghana in a single West African state
questions.D: spurring Nigerian leaders to press Britain for an early date for independence
questions.explanation: At the 1957 and 1958 constitutional conferences Nigerian leaders secured 1 October 1960 as the independence date.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, only adult males in Lagos and Calabar with an annual income of at least one hundred pounds could vote. This franchise was
questions.A: universal, because every Nigerian adult could take part
questions.B: restricted, because it excluded women, the poor and the whole of the North
questions.C: indirect, because chiefs voted on behalf of their people
questions.D: compulsory, because all qualified men were forced to vote
questions.explanation: Only a few thousand men qualified to vote for the four elected seats.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is remembered mainly for
questions.A: abolishing the office of Governor of Nigeria and transferring his powers to an elected prime minister
questions.B: granting Nigeria full internal self-government and fixing a date for the country's independence
questions.C: bringing the North and the South together in one legislature and introducing regionalism
questions.D: creating an executive president for the country and a national assembly with two elected chambers
questions.explanation: For the first time Northern members sat in the Legislative Council in Lagos, while three regional Houses of Assembly were created.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nationalists attacked the Richards Constitution mainly because
questions.A: it abolished the regional Houses of Assembly
questions.B: it gave too much power to the elected Nigerian members
questions.C: it removed the North from the Legislative Council
questions.D: it was imposed without consulting Nigerians and came with unpopular ordinances
questions.explanation: The constitution and the four 'obnoxious ordinances' of 1945 provoked the NCNC's protest tour and London delegation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The consultations held from village to national level before the constitution of 1951 earned it the description of
questions.A: the first constitution written entirely by Nigerians
questions.B: the most democratic of the colonial constitutions in its making
questions.C: the constitution that granted independence to Nigeria
questions.D: the constitution that created the presidential system
questions.explanation: Governor Macpherson's review passed through village, divisional, provincial and regional conferences and the Ibadan General Conference of 1950.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The constitution of 1951 broke down within two years mainly because
questions.A: the North rejected the creation of the House of Representatives
questions.B: the British refused to allow elections under it
questions.C: the regional parties could not work together within its quasi-federal framework
questions.D: the Governor dissolved all the regional assemblies
questions.explanation: The 1953 self-government crisis and the Eastern Regional crisis showed that regional parties would not accept central control.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 differed from earlier constitutions in that it
questions.A: gave the Governor power to legislate for the North alone while the South governed itself through its assembly
questions.B: abolished the regions and created a strong unitary government with a single civil service for the country
questions.C: introduced an executive president elected by the whole country and a bicameral National Assembly
questions.D: established a true federation with regional autonomy and separate regional civil services and judiciaries
questions.explanation: Residual powers went to the regions and Lagos became a federal territory.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Willink Commission of 1957 to 1958, set up to look into the fears of minorities, recommended
questions.A: the immediate creation of the Mid-West, Middle Belt and COR states
questions.B: the inclusion of fundamental human rights in the constitution instead of the creation of new states
questions.C: the abolition of the regions and the creation of twelve states
questions.D: the postponement of independence until minority states were created
questions.explanation: The Commission felt new states would delay independence and proposed rights guarantees and special development boards instead.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the Independence Constitution of 1960, the highest court of appeal for Nigeria was
questions.A: the House of Lords sitting in London
questions.B: the Federal Supreme Court sitting in Lagos
questions.C: the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London
questions.D: the West African Court of Appeal in Accra
questions.explanation: Appeals from the Federal Supreme Court still went to the Privy Council until 1963.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A Nigerian lawyer who in 1964 wished to appeal against a Supreme Court judgment to the Privy Council would have been told that
questions.A: the Privy Council had been replaced by the House of Lords
questions.B: appeals had to go through the Governor-General first
questions.C: the Privy Council only heard appeals from the regions
questions.D: such appeals had been abolished by the Republican Constitution of 1963
questions.explanation: The 1963 constitution made the Supreme Court of Nigeria the final court of appeal.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Constitution Drafting Committee set up by the Murtala Mohammed government in 1975 was chaired by
questions.A: Justice Udo Udoma
questions.B: Chief Rotimi Williams
questions.C: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.D: Justice Akinola Aguda
questions.explanation: The committee of 'forty-nine wise men' produced the draft that the Constituent Assembly under Justice Udo Udoma debated in 1977 to 1978.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Two innovations of the 1979 Constitution were
questions.A: a unicameral National Assembly and a one-party state
questions.B: a parliamentary system and a ceremonial governor-general
questions.C: an executive presidential system and the federal character principle
questions.D: regional premiers and a House of Chiefs in each state
questions.explanation: The 1979 constitution copied the American presidential model and required federal bodies to reflect Nigeria's diversity.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 1989 Constitution never fully came into operation because
questions.A: it was rejected by the voters in a national referendum organised by the National Electoral Commission
questions.B: the Supreme Court declared it null and void on the ground that it had not been approved by the people
questions.C: the National Assembly elected under it refused to ratify it and demanded a return to the 1979 Constitution
questions.D: the transition programme collapsed with the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election
questions.explanation: Parts of it operated for the state and National Assembly elections of 1991 and 1992 before the transition was aborted.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A student claims that the 1999 Constitution was made by an elected assembly of Nigerians. The correct position is that it was
questions.A: adopted by a referendum of all registered voters in 1999
questions.B: promulgated by military decree after a committee collected the views of the public
questions.C: written by the National Assembly elected in February 1999
questions.D: drafted by the United Nations and accepted by Nigeria
questions.explanation: Decree No. 24 of 1999 brought the constitution into force on 29 May 1999 after the Niki Tobi committee's debate.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 provided a House of Chiefs for
questions.A: the Western Region only
questions.B: all three regions
questions.C: the Northern Region only
questions.D: the Eastern Region only
questions.explanation: The West got its House of Chiefs under the 1951 constitution; the East had none until 1959.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Western and Eastern Regions became self-governing in 1957 but the North waited until 1959 because
questions.A: the North was still fighting a civil war in 1957
questions.B: the British refused to grant the North self-government
questions.C: the Northern People's Congress wanted to remain a colony
questions.D: the North asked for more time to train its own people to run the administration
questions.explanation: Northern leaders feared domination by better-educated Southerners in the civil service.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In November 1960 Sir James Robertson was succeeded as Governor-General of Nigeria by
questions.A: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
questions.B: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.C: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.D: Sir Ahmadu Bello
questions.explanation: Azikiwe left the presidency of the Senate to become the first Nigerian Governor-General and, in 1963, the first President.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Senate of the First Republic was made up largely of
questions.A: traditional rulers nominated by the Prime Minister
questions.B: senators directly elected from single-member districts
questions.C: members chosen by the regional legislatures rather than by direct election
questions.D: members elected by the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Each region selected twelve senators; four came from Lagos and four were nominated by the Governor-General, making forty-four.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: A Yoruba trader who had lived in Kano for twenty years could not join the Northern People's Congress in 1960 because
questions.A: the party required members to be university graduates
questions.B: the party accepted only civil servants as members
questions.C: the party had been banned in Kano by the Emir
questions.D: the party's membership was open only to people of Northern origin
questions.explanation: The NPC's restricted membership showed the regional and ethnic character of First Republic parties.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The Action Group was launched in 1951 out of the Egbe Omo Oduduwa mainly in order to
questions.A: unite all the Nigerian parties in a single front against the continuation of colonial rule
questions.B: win the Western Regional elections and keep the NCNC from controlling the West
questions.C: campaign for the creation of the Mid-West Region out of the non-Yoruba areas of the West
questions.D: support the Northern People's Congress in its bid to control the Northern House of Assembly
questions.explanation: Awolowo built the party on the Yoruba cultural organisation to contest the 1951 elections under the new constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The Northern Elements Progressive Union led by Aminu Kano differed from the NPC in that NEPU
questions.A: supported the continuation of British colonial rule until the North had caught up with the South
questions.B: restricted its membership to traditional rulers and the senior officials of the native authorities
questions.C: championed the commoners (talakawa) against the emirs and the Northern aristocracy
questions.D: campaigned for the secession of the Northern Region from Nigeria and the formation of a separate state
questions.explanation: NEPU was a radical party allied to the NCNC, while the NPC was led by the Northern establishment.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: Because no party won a majority in the federal election of 1959,
questions.A: the Action Group formed a minority government with the support of the Governor-General
questions.B: the Governor-General ruled by decree until fresh elections could be held in 1963
questions.C: a fresh election was held before independence to produce a party with a clear majority
questions.D: the NPC and the NCNC formed a coalition government with Balewa as Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The NPC won 134 seats, the NCNC 89 and the AG 73 of the 312 seats; the AG became the opposition.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The Action Group crisis of 1962 arose from
questions.A: a quarrel between Awolowo and Akintola over the choice of the party's running mate for the 1964 federal election
questions.B: a disagreement between Awolowo and Akintola over the party's ideology and whether to join the federal coalition
questions.C: the refusal of the party to accept the results of the 1959 federal election in which it came third
questions.D: the merger of the party with the Northern People's Congress, which the Western members refused to accept
questions.explanation: Awolowo's democratic socialism and opposition role clashed with Premier Akintola's wish to cooperate with the NPC.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: Following the fighting in the Western House of Assembly in May 1962, the Federal Government
questions.A: created the Mid-West Region out of the Western Region in order to weaken the Action Group
questions.B: dissolved the Action Group by decree and arrested all its members in the Western House of Assembly
questions.C: declared a state of emergency in the West and appointed Dr Moses Majekodunmi as administrator
questions.D: held a fresh election in the Western Region immediately under the supervision of the federal police
questions.explanation: The emergency lasted six months, after which Akintola was restored as premier.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: Chief Obafemi Awolowo was tried in 1963 and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment for
questions.A: refusing to hand over as Premier of the Western Region
questions.B: embezzling the funds of the Western Region Marketing Board
questions.C: inciting the riots that followed the 1962 census
questions.D: treasonable felony, that is, plotting to overthrow the federal government
questions.explanation: Awolowo was released by the Gowon government in 1966.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The census controversy of 1962 to 1963 was so bitter because
questions.A: the census was conducted by foreign officials whom Nigerians distrusted
questions.B: population figures determined seats in parliament and revenue shares, so each region wanted a high count
questions.C: the census showed that the population had fallen since 1953
questions.D: the results were used to fix the price of cocoa and groundnuts
questions.explanation: The 1962 count was cancelled and the 1963 figures, which kept the North's majority, were rejected by the East.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: In the federal election of 1964 the United Progressive Grand Alliance (UPGA) consisted of the
questions.A: NPC, NCNC and the Action Group
questions.B: NPC, NNDP and the Niger Delta Congress
questions.C: NCNC, Action Group, NEPU and UMBC
questions.D: NNDP, NEPU and the Dynamic Party
questions.explanation: UPGA faced the Nigerian National Alliance of the NPC, Akintola's NNDP and their allies; UPGA boycotted the election in the East.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The Western Regional election of October 1965 is remembered for
questions.A: the introduction of the secret ballot in Nigeria
questions.B: being the first election in which women in the West voted
questions.C: the peaceful victory of the Action Group over the NNDP
questions.D: widespread rigging and violence that helped to bring about the January 1966 coup
questions.explanation: The 'Operation Wetie' violence that followed the disputed results discredited the First Republic.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The United Middle Belt Congress led by Joseph Tarka campaigned for
questions.A: the merger of the Northern and Western Regions
questions.B: the creation of a Middle Belt state out of the Northern Region
questions.C: the return of the Tiv people to the Eastern Region
questions.D: the abolition of the office of Tor Tiv
questions.explanation: The UMBC allied with the Action Group and Tiv riots broke out in 1960 and 1964.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: In the First Republic, 'carpet-crossing' meant that a legislator
questions.A: was expelled from the house for misconduct
questions.B: refused to attend sittings of the legislature
questions.C: left the party on whose platform he was elected and joined another
questions.D: voted twice on the same motion
questions.explanation: Carpet-crossing changed party strengths in the regional houses without any fresh election.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the collapse of the First Republic?
questions.A: the Action Group crisis and the Western Region emergency
questions.B: the census controversy of 1962 to 1963
questions.C: the rigging of the 1964 federal and 1965 Western elections
questions.D: the adoption of the presidential system of government
questions.explanation: The First Republic operated a parliamentary system; the presidential system came only in 1979.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The motto 'One North, One People, irrespective of religion, rank or tribe' belonged to the
questions.A: Northern Elements Progressive Union
questions.B: Northern People's Congress
questions.C: United Middle Belt Congress
questions.D: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: The NPC under Ahmadu Bello sought to unite the North behind its leadership.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: Dr Michael Okpara became Premier of the Eastern Region in 1959 because Dr Azikiwe
questions.A: lost his seat in the Eastern regional election to a candidate of the Action Group
questions.B: was imprisoned for treasonable felony after the crisis in the Eastern House of Assembly
questions.C: moved to Lagos to become President of the Senate and later Governor-General
questions.D: was appointed Prime Minister of the federation by the Governor-General in that year
questions.explanation: Azikiwe left regional politics for the ceremonial federal posts while Balewa remained Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of military rule?
questions.A: the separation of executive and legislative powers
questions.B: regular elections to choose the head of state
questions.C: the free operation of many political parties
questions.D: government by decrees that oust the jurisdiction of the courts
questions.explanation: Military regimes suspend parts of the constitution, ban parties and legislate by decree.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In May 1966 a decree abolished the regions and merged the regional civil services into one national service. Northern reaction was hostile because
questions.A: the decree transferred the federal capital from Lagos to Enugu against the wishes of the North
questions.B: Northerners feared domination by better-educated Southerners in a unified civil service
questions.C: the decree abolished the emirates and replaced the Islamic courts with magistrates from the South
questions.D: the decree gave the Eastern Region control of the army and the police throughout the federation
questions.explanation: Riots against Decree No. 34 broke out in Northern cities and the decree was repealed after the July 1966 counter-coup.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Aburi Accord of January 1967 failed to prevent the civil war because
questions.A: the Eastern Region rejected the meeting altogether and refused to send any delegation to Ghana for the talks
questions.B: General Ankrah of Ghana, who hosted the meeting, refused to sign the agreement or to guarantee its implementation
questions.C: each side interpreted its terms on regional autonomy differently and Ojukwu rejected the decree that implemented it
questions.D: it required the Eastern Region to pay the full cost of the war and to surrender its oil revenue to the centre
questions.explanation: Ojukwu insisted the accord gave the regions near-confederal powers; Gowon's advisers disagreed and Decree No. 8 fell short of it.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: General Gowon divided the country into twelve states on 27 May 1967 partly in order to
questions.A: give every ethnic group a state of its own
questions.B: punish the North for the riots of 1966
questions.C: carry out a recommendation of the Willink Commission
questions.D: win the support of minorities in the East and weaken the case for secession
questions.explanation: The new states cut the Igbo heartland off from the oil-producing minority areas of the old Eastern Region.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under Gowon, the Supreme Military Council performed the functions of
questions.A: the highest court of appeal in the country, replacing the Supreme Court
questions.B: the highest law-making and policy body, replacing parliament and cabinet
questions.C: the electoral commission responsible for organising elections in the states
questions.D: the council of traditional rulers advising the head of state on customary matters
questions.explanation: The SMC issued decrees; the Federal Executive Council of commissioners handled day-to-day administration.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Gowon's programme of the three Rs after the civil war stood for
questions.A: Recruitment, Retraining and Redeployment
questions.B: Revenue, Roads and Railways
questions.C: Reconciliation, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction
questions.D: Reform, Revolution and Republic
questions.explanation: The programme aimed to reintegrate the former Biafran areas after the 'no victor, no vanquished' declaration of 1970.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: General Gowon was overthrown in July 1975 mainly because
questions.A: he had refused to create any more states despite the demands of the minorities and the advice of his council
questions.B: he had lost the civil war to the Biafran forces and agreed to the division of the country into two states
questions.C: he had handed over power to a civilian government too early, before the army had completed its reforms
questions.D: he had postponed the promised 1976 return to civil rule and failed to curb corruption among the governors
questions.explanation: His October 1974 announcement that 1976 was 'unrealistic' cost him the support of the officer corps.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The regime of General Murtala Mohammed is remembered for
questions.A: the introduction of the Structural Adjustment Programme and the devaluation of the naira against the dollar
questions.B: the purge of the public service, the creation of seven new states and the decision to move the capital to Abuja
questions.C: the promulgation of the 1999 Constitution and the handover of power to an elected civilian government
questions.D: the annulment of a presidential election and the establishment of an interim national government
questions.explanation: In his seven months in office Murtala also set up the Constitution Drafting Committee and announced a 1979 handover date.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The panel whose report led to the choice of Abuja as the new federal capital in 1976 was headed by
questions.A: Justice Udo Udoma
questions.B: Chief Rotimi Williams
questions.C: Justice Akinola Aguda
questions.D: Dr Pius Okigbo
questions.explanation: The Aguda Panel found Lagos congested and recommended a central, ethnically neutral site.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under military rule, the states of Nigeria were administered by
questions.A: commissioners nominated by the traditional rulers
questions.B: governors elected by the people of each state
questions.C: premiers chosen by the state legislatures
questions.D: military governors appointed by the head of state and answerable to him
questions.explanation: Military governors (later administrators) sat on the National Council of States and took orders from the centre.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Obasanjo regime of 1976 to 1979 kept to its transition timetable by
questions.A: postponing the handover date three times before finally leaving office under pressure from the officer corps
questions.B: setting up the Constituent Assembly and FEDECO, lifting the ban on politics in 1978 and handing over in October 1979
questions.C: creating two political parties by decree for the politicians and writing their constitutions and manifestos
questions.D: holding a referendum in which Nigerians voted on whether the military should remain in power or hand over
questions.explanation: The 1979 handover was the first time a Nigerian military regime voluntarily returned power to civilians.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Land Use Decree of 1978 vested all land in each state in
questions.A: the traditional rulers of the state
questions.B: the local government chairmen of the state
questions.C: the governor of the state, to be held in trust for the people
questions.D: the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
questions.explanation: The decree, later entrenched in the constitution, made governors' consent necessary for land transactions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a justification commonly given by soldiers for seizing power?
questions.A: the wish to increase the number of political parties
questions.B: the desire to hold elections more frequently
questions.C: the need to strengthen the independence of the judiciary
questions.D: corruption and the rigging of elections by politicians
questions.explanation: Coup broadcasts in 1966, 1983 and 1985 all cited corruption, indiscipline and electoral fraud.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A lasting negative effect of prolonged military rule on Nigerian federalism is that it
questions.A: gave the states control over the army and the police and left the centre without any security forces
questions.B: concentrated power and revenue at the centre and weakened the autonomy of the states
questions.C: abolished the Federation Account and left the states to depend entirely on internally generated revenue
questions.D: allowed the states to conduct their own foreign policy and to sign treaties with other countries
questions.explanation: The military's chain of command made the states dependent on the centre, a pattern the 1999 Constitution largely kept.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Universal Primary Education scheme launched in September 1976 by the Obasanjo military government aimed to
questions.A: establish a university in each of the nineteen states
questions.B: make secondary education compulsory for all children
questions.C: provide free primary education for every child in the country
questions.D: train soldiers as teachers for the northern states
questions.explanation: UPE greatly increased primary enrolment but was later hampered by a shortage of teachers and funds.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Operation Feed the Nation, launched in 1976, was intended to
questions.A: export Nigerian food crops to neighbouring countries in exchange for oil and machinery
questions.B: distribute free food to soldiers and civil servants in the states affected by the civil war
questions.C: nationalise all the large farms in the country and hand them over to state cooperatives
questions.D: raise food production and reduce food imports by encouraging every citizen to farm
questions.explanation: OFN was followed by the Green Revolution of the Shagari administration in 1980.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 1979 Chief Awolowo went to court arguing that Alhaji Shagari had not scored a quarter of the votes in two-thirds of the nineteen states. The Supreme Court held that
questions.A: Shagari had to face Awolowo in a run-off election within seven days of the announcement of the results
questions.B: two-thirds of nineteen states was twelve and two-thirds states, a requirement that Shagari had satisfied
questions.C: the election must be repeated in all nineteen states because no candidate had met the requirement
questions.D: the electoral college of the National Assembly and the state assemblies should choose the President
questions.explanation: The controversial judgment in Awolowo v. Shagari upheld FEDECO's declaration of Shagari as winner.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The five parties registered by FEDECO for the 1979 elections were the
questions.A: SDP, NRC, PDP, APP and AD
questions.B: NPC, NCNC, AG, NEPU and UMBC
questions.C: NPN, UPN, NPP, GNPP and PRP
questions.D: NPN, UPN, SDP, NRC and NAP
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Advance Party (NAP) was registered later, in 1982, as a sixth party.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The NPN entered into an accord with the NPP in 1979 because
questions.A: the NPP had won the presidential election
questions.B: the constitution required every government to be a coalition
questions.C: the two parties had agreed to merge before the election
questions.D: the NPN lacked a majority in the National Assembly and needed support to pass its bills
questions.explanation: The accord collapsed in 1981 when the NPP withdrew its ministers.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Alhaji Balarabe Musa of Kaduna State, the first Nigerian governor to be impeached, was removed in 1981 mainly because
questions.A: he had been convicted by a court of embezzling state funds and sentenced to a term of imprisonment
questions.B: the NPN-controlled House of Assembly opposed his PRP government and refused to confirm his commissioners
questions.C: he had declared Kaduna State independent of the federation and refused to attend the Council of State
questions.D: the President ordered the state assembly to remove him for failing to implement federal policies
questions.explanation: The impeachment showed how a legislature controlled by a rival party could paralyse a governor.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The economic crisis of the Second Republic from 1981 was caused mainly by
questions.A: a series of strikes by the Nigeria Labour Congress
questions.B: the refusal of the states to pay taxes to the federal government
questions.C: the collapse of world oil prices combined with heavy import-dependent government spending
questions.D: the closure of the Kainji Dam for repairs
questions.explanation: The oil glut cut federal revenue sharply while contracts, imports and salaries had grown during the boom.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Economic Stabilisation (Temporary Provisions) Act of 1982 was introduced to
questions.A: abolish import duties on all goods
questions.B: nationalise the foreign banks operating in Nigeria
questions.C: increase the salaries of public servants
questions.D: cut imports and public spending in response to falling oil revenue
questions.explanation: The austerity measures included import licensing, higher tariffs and a freeze on new projects.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In January 1983 the Shagari government ordered illegal aliens to leave Nigeria. This action is popularly remembered as
questions.A: the closure of the border with Cameroon over the ownership of the Bakassi Peninsula and its oil
questions.B: the 'Ghana Must Go' expulsion of about two million West Africans, most of them Ghanaians
questions.C: the deportation of British managers from the oil companies after the nationalisation of BP
questions.D: the exchange of prisoners with the Republic of Benin after the border clashes of that year
questions.explanation: The expulsion strained relations within ECOWAS, whose protocol allowed free movement of citizens.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The general elections of 1983 contributed to the fall of the Second Republic because
questions.A: they produced a hung National Assembly in which no party was able to form a government
questions.B: they were won by a party that had been deregistered by FEDECO before the elections were held
questions.C: they were massively rigged, producing 'landslide' results that many Nigerians refused to accept
questions.D: they were boycotted by every party except the NPN, leaving the President without an opposition
questions.explanation: Post-election violence in the West and public disillusionment paved the way for the coup of 31 December 1983.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Compared with the First Republic, the system of government of the Second Republic was
questions.A: monarchical, with a ceremonial king
questions.B: parliamentary, with a prime minister chosen by parliament
questions.C: confederal, with regions free to secede
questions.D: presidential, with a directly elected executive president
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution abandoned the Westminster model for an American-style presidency.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Green Revolution programme of the Shagari administration was aimed at
questions.A: planting trees to stop the advance of the desert
questions.B: achieving self-sufficiency in food production
questions.C: building steel plants in the Northern states
questions.D: reducing the number of political parties
questions.explanation: It succeeded Operation Feed the Nation but was undermined by import-dependent schemes and corruption.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Party politics in the Second Republic repeated the pattern of the First Republic in that
questions.A: the parties were created by the government by decree and given their names and manifestos
questions.B: all the major parties were led by former military officers who had taken part in the civil war
questions.C: the major parties drew their support largely from the same regional bases as their predecessors
questions.D: only two parties were allowed by the constitution to contest elections at the federal level
questions.explanation: The NPN inherited the NPC's base, the UPN the AG's and the NPP the NCNC's.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Alhaji Shehu Shagari's running mate in 1979, who served as Vice-President until the coup of December 1983, was
questions.A: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.B: Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.C: Alhaji Waziri Ibrahim
questions.D: Dr Alex Ekwueme
questions.explanation: Ekwueme served as Shagari's Vice-President from 1979 until the coup of December 1983.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the 1979 Constitution the Senate had
questions.A: one hundred and nine members, three from each state
questions.B: ninety-five members, five from each of the nineteen states
questions.C: forty-four members chosen by the states
questions.D: three hundred and sixty members elected by population
questions.explanation: Each of the nineteen states returned five senators, giving a Senate of 95 members.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Second Republic came to an end on 31 December 1983 when
questions.A: the Supreme Court annulled the 1983 elections
questions.B: President Shagari resigned after losing a vote of confidence
questions.C: Major-General Muhammadu Buhari led a coup that overthrew President Shagari
questions.D: President Shagari handed over to General Babangida
questions.explanation: The coup broadcast cited economic mismanagement, corruption and the rigged 1983 elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The War Against Indiscipline launched by the Buhari regime in 1984 aimed to
questions.A: close down all private newspapers in the country
questions.B: recruit young men into the army to fight in Chad
questions.C: punish civil servants who had served under Shagari
questions.D: instil orderliness, punctuality, patriotism and honesty in public life
questions.explanation: Queuing at bus stops and the singing of the national anthem in schools were features of WAI.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Decree No. 4 of 1984 restricted press freedom because it
questions.A: required newspapers to publish only press releases issued by the government and the armed forces
questions.B: made it an offence to publish any report that embarrassed a public officer, even if it was true
questions.C: banned the importation of newsprint into the country and closed the mills that produced it locally
questions.D: gave the government ownership of all radio and television stations and the major newspapers
questions.explanation: Two Guardian journalists, Tunde Thompson and Nduka Irabor, were jailed under the decree.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Buhari regime changed the colour of the naira notes in 1984 in order to
questions.A: make the naira equal in value to the British pound
questions.B: celebrate the silver jubilee of Nigeria's independence
questions.C: trap illegally held currency and curb currency trafficking across the borders
questions.D: introduce coins in place of all paper money
questions.explanation: Borders were closed during the exchange and limits were placed on the amount each person could change.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Babangida regime departed from its predecessor's economic policy by
questions.A: abolishing the naira and adopting the CFA franc in a monetary union with Nigeria's francophone neighbours
questions.B: nationalising all the foreign companies in the country and placing them under military management
questions.C: fixing the prices of all essential commodities by decree and prosecuting traders who exceeded them
questions.D: adopting the Structural Adjustment Programme in 1986 after a national debate had rejected an IMF loan
questions.explanation: SAP devalued the naira, removed subsidies and liberalised trade in line with IMF and World Bank conditions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Political Bureau set up by Babangida in 1986 was asked to
questions.A: draft a new constitution for the Third Republic and submit it to a national referendum for approval
questions.B: collect the views of Nigerians on a suitable political system for the next civilian government
questions.C: conduct the elections into the state assemblies and the National Assembly under the transition
questions.D: investigate the assets of the politicians of the Second Republic and recover stolen public funds
questions.explanation: The Bureau, chaired by Dr S. J. Cookey, recommended among other things a two-party system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 1989 the Babangida government refused to register any of the thirteen political associations that applied and instead
questions.A: allowed the old parties of the Second Republic to return
questions.B: postponed the transition programme indefinitely
questions.C: created two parties, the SDP and the NRC, and wrote their constitutions and manifestos
questions.D: registered only the association with the largest membership
questions.explanation: The government argued that the associations were fronts for old politicians and ethnic interests.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: MAMSER, established in 1987, was designed to
questions.A: collect taxes from traders in the informal sector
questions.B: supervise the privatisation of public enterprises
questions.C: recruit graduates into the National Youth Service Corps
questions.D: educate and mobilise Nigerians politically for the transition to civil rule
questions.explanation: The Directorate for Social Mobilisation ran campaigns on voting, self-reliance and social justice.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: General Babangida 'stepped aside' in August 1993 after
questions.A: the Supreme Court ordered him to leave office and hand over to the winner of the presidential election
questions.B: the annulment of the June 12 presidential election provoked nationwide protests and strikes
questions.C: a coup led by General Abacha removed him from office and forced him to leave the country
questions.D: he lost a national referendum on whether he should continue in office until 1997
questions.explanation: He handed over to an Interim National Government under Chief Ernest Shonekan.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Abacha regime became internationally isolated after
questions.A: it refused to join the Organisation of the Islamic Conference
questions.B: it withdrew Nigerian troops from Liberia
questions.C: the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists in November 1995
questions.D: it handed over power to civilians too quickly
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth suspended Nigeria and several countries imposed sanctions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The six states created by General Abacha in October 1996 brought the number of states in Nigeria to
questions.explanation: Ebonyi, Bayelsa, Nasarawa, Gombe, Ekiti and Zamfara were added to the thirty states created by Babangida.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The five political parties registered under Abacha in 1996 were mocked as 'five fingers of a leprous hand' because
questions.A: each of them was led by a serving military officer
questions.B: all of them adopted Abacha as their sole presidential candidate
questions.C: they were all based in the Northern states
questions.D: none of them was allowed to hold rallies
questions.explanation: The adoption exposed the transition as a plan for Abacha to succeed himself; he died in June 1998.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: General Abdulsalami Abubakar's transition programme succeeded mainly because
questions.A: it kept all the politicians of the Second Republic out of politics and allowed only new candidates to stand
questions.B: it created two political parties by decree and wrote their manifestos so that the politicians could not quarrel
questions.C: it was short, released political prisoners and allowed INEC to conduct elections within eleven months
questions.D: it was supervised from beginning to end by the United Nations, which conducted and counted the elections
questions.explanation: Abubakar handed over to President Obasanjo on 29 May 1999, barely a year after taking office.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Petroleum (Special) Trust Fund set up under Abacha was financed from
questions.A: fines imposed on politicians of the Second Republic
questions.B: grants from the World Bank and the IMF
questions.C: the sale of the government's shares in the oil companies
questions.D: the proceeds of the 1994 increase in the pump price of petrol
questions.explanation: The PTF, chaired by General Buhari, spent the money on roads, health and education projects.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Decree No. 2 of 1984 on state security allowed the government to
questions.A: try civilians in military courts for traffic offences
questions.B: detain persons without trial for renewable periods on security grounds
questions.C: seize the property of foreign companies
questions.D: dismiss judges without any reason
questions.explanation: The decree ousted the jurisdiction of the courts and was used against politicians, journalists and activists.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) formed in 1994 demanded
questions.A: the payment of pensions to retired soldiers
questions.B: the creation of more states in the South-West
questions.C: the recognition of the June 12 mandate and the withdrawal of the military from politics
questions.D: a return to the parliamentary system of the First Republic
questions.explanation: NADECO's leaders were harassed and some fled into exile during the Abacha years.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the Third Republic transition, the SDP was described by the government as 'a little to the left' and the NRC as 'a little to the right'. This shows that the parties were
questions.A: formed by trade unions and business associations
questions.B: the same parties that had existed in the Second Republic
questions.C: based on the ethnic groups of their founders
questions.D: created by the government with imposed ideologies rather than formed by the people
questions.explanation: The government even built their secretariats and funded them, calling them 'grassroots' parties.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Between 1992 and 1993 elected civilian governors and legislatures operated under a military president. This arrangement is described as
questions.A: confederation
questions.B: diarchy
questions.C: oligarchy
questions.D: plutocracy
questions.explanation: Diarchy is the sharing of government between the military and civilians.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Chief M. K. O. Abiola's choice of Alhaji Babagana Kingibe as running mate in 1993 was remarkable because
questions.A: Kingibe had been the presidential candidate of the NRC
questions.B: Kingibe was a serving military officer
questions.C: both were Muslims, yet the ticket won votes across religious and regional lines
questions.D: both came from the same local government area
questions.explanation: The Muslim-Muslim ticket won even in Tofa's home state of Kano.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The presidential election of June 12, 1993 is regarded as the freest and fairest in Nigeria's history mainly because
questions.A: every registered voter in the country took part in it and all of them voted for the same candidate
questions.B: it was conducted by the United Nations and monitored by soldiers from other African countries
questions.C: only one candidate contested it, so there was no dispute about who had won the election
questions.D: its results cut across ethnic and religious lines and there was little evidence of rigging
questions.explanation: The election used the open-secret ballot and was conducted by the National Electoral Commission under Professor Humphrey Nwosu.

questions.subject: Government
