questions.q: The announcement of the results of the June 12, 1993 election was halted after
questions.A: the SDP withdrew from the election and asked its supporters not to accept any of the results announced
questions.B: an injunction obtained by the Association for Better Nigeria and the annulment by the Babangida government
questions.C: the NRC candidate conceded defeat before the counting was complete and asked for the results to be withheld
questions.D: a fire destroyed the ballot papers at the headquarters of the National Electoral Commission in Abuja
questions.explanation: Senator Arthur Nzeribe's ABN obtained the injunction; the government annulled the election on 23 June 1993.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Interim National Government headed by Chief Ernest Shonekan was
questions.A: the government formed by the winner of the June 12 election after the results were finally announced
questions.B: elected by the National Assembly in 1993 to serve until a new presidential election could be held
questions.C: set up by Babangida in August 1993 and declared illegal by a Lagos High Court in November 1993
questions.D: a military government led by General Abacha with Chief Shonekan as its civilian chairman
questions.explanation: Justice Dolapo Akinsanya's judgment weakened the ING and General Abacha took over on 17 November 1993.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: 'Option A4' in the 1993 presidential primaries referred to
questions.A: the fourth draft constitution prepared for the Third Republic by the Constitution Review Committee
questions.B: the fourth attempt by the military government to hand over power to an elected civilian administration
questions.C: the design of the ballot paper used on election day, with four columns for the four stages of voting
questions.D: an open primary system in which candidates emerged through ward, local government, state and national stages
questions.explanation: Option A4 was adopted after the cancellation of the 1992 primaries.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Senate President of the National Assembly inaugurated in December 1992 was
questions.A: Chief Anthony Anenih
questions.B: Dr Iyorchia Ayu
questions.C: Alhaji Bashir Tofa
questions.D: Dr Joseph Wayas
questions.explanation: The Assembly sat for less than a year before the transition was aborted.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Campaign for Democracy led by Dr Beko Ransome-Kuti was prominent in 1993 for
questions.A: campaigning for the NRC presidential candidate
questions.B: supporting the military government's transition programme
questions.C: organising mass protests against the annulment of the June 12 election
questions.D: demanding the creation of new states in the North
questions.explanation: The protests in Lagos and other cities in July 1993 forced Babangida to leave office in August.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Babangida transition programme is described as 'endless' because
questions.A: it was handled by three different electoral commissions
questions.B: it lasted only a few months
questions.C: it was completed ahead of schedule
questions.D: the handover date was shifted several times, from 1990 to 1992 and then to 1993
questions.explanation: Each shift was justified by the need to perfect the process, but critics accused Babangida of wanting to stay in power.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: After declaring himself President at Epetedo, Lagos, on 11 June 1994, Chief Abiola was
questions.A: sworn in as President by the Chief Justice of Nigeria at a ceremony in Abuja
questions.B: arrested, charged with treason and detained until his death in July 1998
questions.C: appointed Vice-President by General Abacha in a government of national unity
questions.D: allowed to leave the country and lived in exile in London until his death
questions.explanation: Abiola died in detention on 7 July 1998, a month after Abacha's death.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following distinguishes the Third Republic from the First and Second Republics?
questions.A: it had more than five registered political parties competing freely for power at every level
questions.B: it operated a parliamentary system of government with a prime minister chosen by the legislature
questions.C: it never had an elected civilian president because the presidential election was annulled
questions.D: it lasted longer than either of the other two republics before being ended by a military coup
questions.explanation: Only state governments and the National Assembly of the Third Republic ever functioned.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The ban placed on 'old breed' politicians during the Babangida transition was intended to
questions.A: reduce the cost of conducting elections
questions.B: reserve political office for retired military officers
questions.C: prevent Southerners from contesting the presidency
questions.D: bring in 'new breed' politicians untainted by the failures of earlier republics
questions.explanation: The ban was later lifted, and many old politicians re-entered through proxies anyway.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Fourth Republic began on 29 May 1999 when
questions.A: General Abacha handed over power to Chief Ernest Shonekan as head of an interim national government
questions.B: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as elected President after a handover by General Abubakar
questions.C: the results of the June 12 presidential election were finally announced and the winner sworn in
questions.D: Alhaji Shehu Shagari returned to office after the Supreme Court annulled the coup that removed him
questions.explanation: 29 May was Democracy Day until 2018; from 2019 the day has been marked on June 12 instead.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The three parties registered for the 1999 elections were the
questions.A: SDP, NRC and NAP
questions.B: NPN, UPN and NPP
questions.C: PDP, APP and AD
questions.D: APC, PDP and LP
questions.explanation: The People's Democratic Party won the presidency; the All People's Party and the Alliance for Democracy fielded a joint candidate.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 'doctrine of necessity' resolution passed by the National Assembly in February 2010 was used to
questions.A: postpone the 2011 general elections until the voters' register had been completely revised
questions.B: extend the tenure of the National Assembly by two years because of the security situation
questions.C: remove the Chief Justice of Nigeria from office without following the procedure in the constitution
questions.D: make Vice-President Goodluck Jonathan Acting President during President Yar'Adua's illness
questions.explanation: Yar'Adua had not formally transmitted a letter handing over power before travelling abroad for treatment.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The presidential election of 2015 was historic because
questions.A: it was the first election conducted by INEC since the return to civilian rule in 1999
questions.B: an opposition candidate defeated a sitting president for the first time and the loser conceded peacefully
questions.C: it produced the first civilian president since the military coup of January 1966
questions.D: it was the first election in which women in the Northern states were allowed to vote
questions.explanation: President Jonathan telephoned General Buhari to concede before the final results were announced.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The All Progressives Congress was formed in 2013 through
questions.A: a decree of the federal government
questions.B: the renaming of the People's Democratic Party
questions.C: the merger of the ACN, CPC, ANPP and a faction of APGA
questions.D: the revival of the Second Republic's NPN
questions.explanation: The merger united the main opposition parties ahead of the 2015 elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Not Too Young To Run Act of 2018 reduced the minimum age for
questions.A: membership of the Senate from thirty-five to thirty years and of state assemblies to twenty-one
questions.B: voting in all elections from eighteen to sixteen years so that senior secondary students could take part
questions.C: appointment as a minister or commissioner from thirty-five to thirty years and as a judge to forty
questions.D: contesting the presidency from forty to thirty-five and the House of Representatives from thirty to twenty-five
questions.explanation: The Act amended the 1999 Constitution after a campaign by youth groups; the Senate age was unchanged.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Electoral Act of 2022 is associated with
questions.A: the creation of the Independent National Electoral Commission
questions.B: legal backing for electronic accreditation of voters and electronic transmission of results
questions.C: the introduction of the two-party system
questions.D: the return of the open ballot system
questions.explanation: The Act underpinned the use of BVAS and the IReV result-viewing portal in the 2023 elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The failed 'third term agenda' of 2006 referred to
questions.A: a proposal by the military to remain in power for three more years before handing over to civilians
questions.B: a plan to extend the school year from two terms to three terms in all federal government colleges
questions.C: an attempt to amend the constitution to allow the President and governors a third term, rejected by the Senate
questions.D: the third attempt to conduct a national population census after the failures of 1962 and 1973
questions.explanation: The Senate threw out the amendment bill in May 2006, upholding the two-term limit.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was set up in the Fourth Republic to
questions.A: audit the accounts of the National Assembly and report on the spending of the legislators
questions.B: collect taxes on behalf of the federal government and prosecute those who evade payment
questions.C: regulate the activities of commercial banks and protect the deposits of their customers
questions.D: investigate and prosecute financial crimes such as money laundering and advance fee fraud
questions.explanation: The EFCC and the ICPC (2000) are the Fourth Republic's main anti-corruption agencies.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The adoption of Sharia criminal law by twelve Northern states from 1999 raised constitutional debate about
questions.A: the power of the states to create local governments
questions.B: the provision that no government shall adopt any religion as a state religion
questions.C: the right of the National Assembly to make laws on defence
questions.D: the tenure of state governors
questions.explanation: Section 10 of the 1999 Constitution forbids a state religion; supporters argued that the states were exercising residual powers.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Niger Delta amnesty programme of 2009 was introduced by
questions.A: General Abacha to end the Ogoni crisis
questions.B: President Obasanjo to punish the militants who attacked oil installations
questions.C: President Umaru Yar'Adua to end militancy by offering pardon, training and stipends to ex-militants
questions.D: President Buhari to disarm Boko Haram fighters
questions.explanation: The programme sharply reduced attacks on oil facilities and raised oil production.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Compared with the First and Second Republics, the Fourth Republic is notable for
questions.A: operating a one-party system in which only the ruling party is allowed to contest elections
questions.B: having a parliamentary system of government with a prime minister drawn from the legislature
questions.C: being brought to an end by a military coup after less than five years of civilian government
questions.D: its longevity, with regular elections and civilian-to-civilian transfers of power since 1999
questions.explanation: Power has changed hands between parties and presidents without military intervention.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 2023 the Supreme Court ruled that a presidential candidate need not score a quarter of the votes in the Federal Capital Territory because
questions.A: the FCT has no registered voters of its own because its residents vote in their states of origin
questions.B: the FCT is treated as if it were a state, so it is only one of thirty-seven units for the spread requirement
questions.C: votes cast in the FCT are counted only if a run-off election becomes necessary between the leading candidates
questions.D: the FCT belongs to Niger State for electoral purposes and its votes are added to those of that state
questions.explanation: The court rejected the argument that the FCT enjoyed a special status in the 25 per cent spread rule.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The impeachment of Governor Rashidi Ladoja of Oyo State in 2006 was reversed by the Supreme Court because
questions.A: governors cannot be impeached during their first term
questions.B: the President had not approved the impeachment
questions.C: the state assembly had not followed the procedure laid down in the constitution
questions.D: the governor had already resigned from office
questions.explanation: Only eighteen of thirty-two legislators, meeting outside the assembly, had voted for removal; two-thirds are required.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution a person may be elected President of Nigeria for
questions.A: a maximum of three terms of four years each
questions.B: one term of six years only
questions.C: as many terms as the electorate wishes
questions.D: a maximum of two terms of four years each
questions.explanation: Section 137 disqualifies anyone who has been elected to the office twice.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's federal system had its origins in
questions.A: the presidential system introduced in 1979 and the creation of nineteen states by the military
questions.B: the regionalism of the Richards Constitution and the federal structure of the Lyttleton Constitution
questions.C: the creation of twelve states by General Gowon in 1967 on the eve of the civil war
questions.D: the amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914 by Lord Lugard
questions.explanation: Regionalism in 1946 grew into three autonomous regions in 1954.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria adopted federalism at independence mainly because
questions.A: all its neighbours operated federal systems
questions.B: the British insisted on it as a condition for independence
questions.C: its size and ethnic diversity made a unitary system unacceptable to the regions
questions.D: the leaders wanted to copy the Soviet Union
questions.explanation: Each of the three major groups feared domination by the others in a unitary state.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's federation is often said to have unitary features because
questions.A: the President is elected by the state governors rather than by the people of the whole country
questions.B: the states have their own armies and currencies and conduct their own relations with other countries
questions.C: the constitution allows any state to secede from the federation after a referendum of its people
questions.D: the centre controls most of the revenue, the police and the creation of states and local governments
questions.explanation: Decades of military rule strengthened the centre at the expense of the states.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following items is on the exclusive legislative list under the 1999 Constitution?
questions.A: markets, motor parks and cemeteries
questions.B: defence, currency and external affairs
questions.C: primary education and refuse disposal
questions.D: chieftaincy matters and customary land
questions.explanation: Only the National Assembly may legislate on exclusive-list items; the others are state or local government matters.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The federal character principle is applied in Nigeria mainly through
questions.A: the rotation of the presidency among the six geopolitical zones by law
questions.B: the equal division of oil revenue among all citizens
questions.C: quotas in appointments to federal bodies and admissions to federal institutions
questions.D: the appointment of traditional rulers to the Senate
questions.explanation: The Federal Character Commission monitors compliance; zoning of the presidency is a party practice, not law.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A persistent problem of Nigerian federalism is
questions.A: the equal size and population of all the states, which makes it impossible to share revenue fairly
questions.B: the absence of a written constitution setting out the powers of the federal and state governments
questions.C: the lack of a Supreme Court with power to settle disputes between the centre and the states
questions.D: the dispute over revenue allocation between the oil-producing states and the rest of the federation
questions.explanation: Derivation, population and equality of states have been fought over since the Phillipson Commission of 1946.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The derivation principle in the 1999 Constitution requires that
questions.A: all revenue from crude oil be shared equally among the thirty-six states regardless of where it is produced
questions.B: not less than thirteen per cent of revenue from natural resources be paid to the states from which the resources come
questions.C: the federal government keep all revenue from natural resources and share only the proceeds of taxation
questions.D: local governments receive half of all mining royalties and pay the remainder into the Federation Account
questions.explanation: Section 162(2) fixes the minimum at 13 per cent; derivation had been 50 per cent in the 1960s.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The only region or state created under a civilian government in Nigeria's history is
questions.A: Bayelsa State in 1996
questions.B: Lagos State in 1967
questions.C: the Mid-West Region in 1963
questions.D: Kwara State in 1967
questions.explanation: All later states were created by military decree in 1967, 1976, 1987, 1991 and 1996.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The National Youth Service Corps, established in 1973, was designed to
questions.A: employ youths on federal road projects
questions.B: provide military training for all secondary school leavers
questions.C: recruit graduates into the federal civil service
questions.D: promote national unity by posting graduates to serve in states other than their own
questions.explanation: The scheme was part of Gowon's post-war reconciliation and integration policy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The body that advises on the formula for sharing revenue among the three tiers of government in Nigeria is the
questions.A: Federation Account Allocation Committee
questions.B: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
questions.C: Federal Character Commission
questions.D: Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.explanation: RMAFC also fixes the remuneration of political office holders.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The agitation for 'true federalism' or restructuring in Nigeria refers to demands for
questions.A: the merger of the states into the old regions only
questions.B: the return of the military to power
questions.C: the devolution of more powers and resources from the centre to the states
questions.D: the abolition of the Senate
questions.explanation: Proposals include state police, resource control and a shorter exclusive list.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Unlike the thirty-six states, the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, is administered by
questions.A: the Emir of Suleja under a treaty of 1976
questions.B: a governor elected by the residents
questions.C: the Senate President on behalf of the National Assembly
questions.D: a minister appointed by the President rather than an elected governor
questions.explanation: The National Assembly acts as the legislature for the FCT.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's federation differs from that of the United States in that
questions.A: the Nigerian states have larger populations and territories than any of the American states
questions.B: the Nigerian states were created by the centre and never existed as independent units
questions.C: Nigeria has no written constitution dividing powers between the centre and the states
questions.D: the American states have no legislatures or governors of their own and are ruled from Washington
questions.explanation: The American union was formed by previously independent states; Nigeria's was created by devolution from a colonial centre.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Policing in Nigeria is on the exclusive legislative list, which means that
questions.A: local governments recruit and pay their own police
questions.B: each state controls its own police commissioner
questions.C: there is a single national police force and states cannot create their own
questions.D: traditional rulers command the police in their domains
questions.explanation: The debate over state police is part of the wider restructuring debate.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Fiscal federalism in Nigeria is criticised because
questions.A: local governments receive more revenue than the states and the federal government combined
questions.B: the states collect all the taxes in the country and pay nothing into the Federation Account
questions.C: the federal government has no revenue of its own and depends on contributions from the states
questions.D: most states depend heavily on federal allocations rather than on internally generated revenue
questions.explanation: Monthly allocations from the Federation Account make up the bulk of most state budgets.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's foreign policy has long made Africa its 'centrepiece'. This means that
questions.A: Nigeria has no diplomatic relations with any country outside Africa and belongs to no non-African body
questions.B: African issues such as decolonisation and the fight against apartheid have had the first claim on its attention
questions.C: Nigeria's embassies and high commissions are located only in African capitals and nowhere else
questions.D: Nigeria trades exclusively with other African countries and refuses to import goods from Europe or Asia
questions.explanation: Concentric circles of interest place Nigeria's neighbours first, then West Africa, then Africa, then the world.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Non-alignment as a principle of Nigeria's foreign policy meant that Nigeria
questions.A: refused to trade with any communist country or to accept aid from the Soviet bloc
questions.B: did not belong to any international organisation during the Cold War years
questions.C: refused to join either the Western or the Eastern bloc during the Cold War
questions.D: kept its army out of all peace-keeping operations organised by the United Nations
questions.explanation: In practice Balewa's government leaned towards the West, but Nigeria joined the Non-Aligned Movement in 1964.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France in January 1961 because
questions.A: France tested an atomic bomb in the Sahara despite Nigeria's protests
questions.B: France supported Biafra during the civil war
questions.C: France refused to grant independence to Dahomey
questions.D: France closed its embassy in Lagos
questions.explanation: The break lasted until 1965 and showed the new state's independence in foreign affairs.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Anglo-Nigerian Defence Pact of 1960 was abrogated in 1962 because
questions.A: students and nationalists protested that it compromised Nigeria's independence and non-alignment
questions.B: Britain refused to supply the arms and training that it had promised Nigeria under the pact
questions.C: the pact had been signed for a fixed period of two years and simply expired at the end of 1962
questions.D: the United States asked Nigeria to cancel it and to sign a new defence agreement with Washington
questions.explanation: Demonstrations in Lagos forced Balewa's government to abandon the pact.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: General Murtala Mohammed's declaration that 'Africa has come of age' at the OAU summit of January 1976 concerned
questions.A: Nigeria's recognition of the MPLA government in Angola in defiance of American pressure
questions.B: the creation of ECOWAS at the Lagos summit of West African heads of state in 1975
questions.C: the decision to move the federal capital from Lagos to a new city at Abuja
questions.D: Nigeria's admission into OPEC as the organisation's eleventh member state
questions.explanation: Nigeria's support swung the OAU behind the MPLA against the South African-backed UNITA.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Obasanjo military government nationalised the Nigerian assets of British Petroleum in 1979 in order to
questions.A: pressure Britain over the independence of Zimbabwe and its links with apartheid South Africa
questions.B: raise the money needed to pay for the 1979 general elections and the handover to civilians
questions.C: punish BP for polluting the creeks and farmlands of the Niger Delta over many years
questions.D: hand the company over to Nigerian workers as part of the indigenisation programme
questions.explanation: The move, just before the Commonwealth summit in Lusaka, helped push Britain towards the Lancaster House settlement.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: When world oil prices collapsed in 2016, Nigeria found it harder to fund its embassies and peace-keeping commitments abroad. This illustrates that a country's foreign policy is shaped by
questions.A: its economic strength and the sources of its revenue
questions.B: the size of its film and music industries
questions.C: the number of universities in the country
questions.D: the number of languages spoken within its borders
questions.explanation: Economic factors, population, military strength, history, geography and leadership all shape foreign policy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Technical Aid Corps scheme established in 1987 is an instrument of foreign policy under which Nigeria
questions.A: sends Nigerian professionals to serve in African, Caribbean and Pacific countries
questions.B: receives technical experts from developed countries
questions.C: gives scholarships to Nigerian students to study abroad
questions.D: exports arms to friendly African governments
questions.explanation: TAC volunteers such as doctors and teachers serve two-year terms as a form of South-South cooperation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: 'Economic diplomacy' under the Babangida administration meant
questions.A: using foreign relations to attract investment, expand trade and secure debt relief
questions.B: closing Nigeria's borders to all foreign goods in order to protect local industries
questions.C: giving economic aid to every African country in order to win their support at the OAU
questions.D: leaving all international economic organisations that imposed conditions on Nigeria
questions.explanation: The policy accompanied the Structural Adjustment Programme and its search for foreign investment.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's leading role in ECOMOG in Liberia from 1990 and Sierra Leone from 1997 reflected its foreign policy principle of
questions.A: promoting peace and security in West Africa as its immediate neighbourhood
questions.B: non-interference in the internal affairs of other states, however troubled
questions.C: isolation from regional conflicts in order to concentrate on domestic problems
questions.D: alignment with the Soviet bloc in the conflicts of the West African sub-region
questions.explanation: Nigeria provided most of the troops and funds for the ECOWAS Monitoring Group.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 2005 Nigeria secured the cancellation of about eighteen billion dollars of its foreign debt from
questions.A: the Paris Club of creditor nations
questions.B: the African Development Bank
questions.C: the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
questions.D: the Commonwealth Secretariat
questions.explanation: The deal negotiated under President Obasanjo and Finance Minister Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala cleared most of Nigeria's external debt.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 'citizen diplomacy' announced under President Yar'Adua emphasised
questions.A: the protection of Nigerians abroad and reciprocity in the treatment of Nigerian citizens
questions.B: the right of foreigners resident in Nigeria to become Nigerian citizens after five years
questions.C: the recruitment of Nigerians living abroad into the diplomatic service as honorary consuls
questions.D: the withdrawal of Nigeria from the United Nations in protest at the treatment of its citizens
questions.explanation: The policy responded to complaints of maltreatment of Nigerians in other countries.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria boycotted the Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh in 1986 in order to
questions.A: protest against Britain's refusal to impose sanctions on apartheid South Africa
questions.B: protest against the suspension of Nigerian athletes for doping
questions.C: save money during the economic crisis
questions.D: support the Soviet boycott of Western sporting events
questions.explanation: Nigeria led a boycott of thirty-two countries, mostly African, Asian and Caribbean.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Section 19 of the 1999 Constitution lists Nigeria's foreign policy objectives, which include
questions.A: the promotion of African integration and support for African unity
questions.B: the annexation of neighbouring territories
questions.C: the establishment of military bases in West Africa
questions.D: the withdrawal of Nigeria from the United Nations
questions.explanation: The section also mentions respect for international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's first substantive Minister of Foreign Affairs, appointed in 1961, was
questions.A: Jaja Wachuku
questions.B: Joseph Garba
questions.C: Bolaji Akinyemi
questions.D: Okoi Arikpo
questions.explanation: Balewa held the portfolio himself at independence before appointing Wachuku.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Ghana's Aliens Compliance Order of 1969 affected Nigeria because
questions.A: it led to the expulsion of many Nigerians living and trading in Ghana
questions.B: it closed the border between Nigeria and Ghana
questions.C: it banned Ghanaian traders from entering Nigeria
questions.D: it made Nigerians in Ghana automatic citizens
questions.explanation: Nigeria's own expulsion of illegal aliens in 1983 was seen by many Ghanaians as revenge.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Relations between Nigeria and Britain were badly strained in 1984 by
questions.A: the attempt to smuggle Umaru Dikko out of London in a crate
questions.B: Britain's recognition of Biafra as an independent state
questions.C: the nationalisation of Barclays Bank by the Buhari regime
questions.D: Britain's refusal to send a delegation to FESTAC in Lagos
questions.explanation: The Buhari regime's attempt to abduct the former minister led both countries to withdraw their high commissioners.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon over the Bakassi Peninsula was finally resolved through
questions.A: the International Court of Justice judgment of 2002 and the Green Tree Agreement of 2006
questions.B: a war in which the Nigerian army captured the whole peninsula and expelled the Cameroonian forces
questions.C: a decision of the ECOWAS Court of Justice sitting in Abuja, which both countries accepted
questions.D: a referendum organised by the African Union in which the people of Bakassi chose Nigeria
questions.explanation: Nigeria handed over Bakassi to Cameroon in August 2008 in line with the agreement.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria recalled its ambassador from Libya in 2010 after
questions.A: Colonel Gaddafi suggested that Nigeria should be divided into Christian and Muslim states
questions.B: Libya expelled thousands of Nigerian migrant workers and seized their property without compensation
questions.C: Libya supported Cameroon's claim to the Bakassi Peninsula at the International Court of Justice
questions.D: Libya refused to pay its dues to OPEC and accused Nigeria of exceeding its production quota
questions.explanation: The Senate described Gaddafi's remarks as an incitement to disintegration.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: During the civil war the Soviet Union
questions.A: supplied aircraft and arms to the federal side after Britain and the United States hesitated
questions.B: recognised Biafra as an independent state and sent it military advisers and heavy weapons
questions.C: imposed an arms embargo on both sides and closed its embassy in Lagos for the duration of the war
questions.D: mediated the peace talks between the two sides at Kampala and Addis Ababa
questions.explanation: Soviet MiG fighters and Ilyushin bombers helped the federal air force; the relationship later produced the Ajaokuta steel project.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with Israel in 1973
questions.A: in line with an OAU resolution after the Arab-Israeli war, and restored them in 1992
questions.B: because Israel had supported Biafra during the civil war, and never restored them
questions.C: after Israel closed its embassy in Lagos and expelled the Nigerian ambassador from Tel Aviv
questions.D: because Israel refused to sell arms to Nigeria, and restored them the following year
questions.explanation: Most African states cut ties with Israel in 1973 in solidarity with Egypt.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Relations between Nigeria and South Africa since 1994 have been disturbed mainly by
questions.A: xenophobic attacks on Nigerians and other Africans in South Africa
questions.B: disputes over the ownership of Bakassi
questions.C: South Africa's refusal to join the African Union
questions.D: Nigeria's support for the apartheid government
questions.explanation: After the 2019 attacks Nigeria evacuated hundreds of its citizens from South Africa.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In August 2019 Nigeria closed its land borders with Benin and Niger in order to
questions.A: curb the smuggling of rice, other goods and arms into the country
questions.B: prevent the spread of the Ebola virus
questions.C: stop Nigerians from travelling to Europe by road
questions.D: force the two countries to adopt the naira
questions.explanation: The closure was criticised as a breach of the ECOWAS protocol on free movement of goods and persons.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria cooperates with Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Benin in the Multinational Joint Task Force in order to
questions.A: fight Boko Haram and other insurgents around the Lake Chad basin
questions.B: patrol the waters of the Gulf of Guinea against pirates and oil thieves
questions.C: share the waters of the River Niger and Lake Chad for irrigation
questions.D: collect customs duties jointly at the border posts between the countries
questions.explanation: The force is headquartered in N'Djamena, Chad.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's relationship with China since 2000 has been marked by
questions.A: Chinese loans and contractors for railways, airports and power projects
questions.B: the establishment of Nigerian military bases in China and joint naval exercises
questions.C: a Chinese boycott of Nigerian crude oil in favour of supplies from the Middle East
questions.D: the adoption of Chinese as an official language in Nigerian secondary schools
questions.explanation: The Abuja-Kaduna and Lagos-Ibadan railways were built by Chinese firms with Chinese loans.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The plebiscite held in the British Cameroons in 1961 resulted in
questions.A: the Northern Cameroons joining Nigeria and the Southern Cameroons joining the Republic of Cameroon
questions.B: the whole territory joining Nigeria as a fourth region with its own premier and House of Assembly
questions.C: the whole territory becoming an independent state with its capital at Buea under a British governor
questions.D: the territory remaining a United Nations trust territory under British administration until 1975
questions.explanation: The Northern Cameroons became the Sardauna Province of Northern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Relations between Nigeria and the United States during the Abacha years were marked by
questions.A: American sanctions and the decertification of Nigeria over drug trafficking and human rights
questions.B: a joint military alliance against Libya and the stationing of American troops in Nigeria
questions.C: the establishment of American military bases in Nigeria to protect the oil installations
questions.D: the cancellation of Nigeria's debts by the United States and a large increase in American aid
questions.explanation: Relations improved after 1999, with President Clinton visiting Nigeria in 2000.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's relations with its French-speaking neighbours have sometimes been difficult because
questions.A: their close ties with France and use of the CFA franc create a rival bloc within ECOWAS
questions.B: they refuse to trade with Nigeria at all and have closed their borders to Nigerian goods
questions.C: they share no borders with Nigeria and have little contact with Nigerian traders and travellers
questions.D: they belong to the Commonwealth rather than ECOWAS and follow British rather than French policies
questions.explanation: The francophone states formed UEMOA and CEAO, which Nigeria saw as competing with ECOWAS.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 1976 relations between Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea were strained by
questions.A: the maltreatment of Nigerian plantation workers on the island of Fernando Po
questions.B: Equatorial Guinea's claim to the Bakassi Peninsula
questions.C: the closure of the Nigerian embassy in Malabo by Nigeria
questions.D: Equatorial Guinea's support for the Biafran cause
questions.explanation: Nigeria evacuated its citizens after reports of killings and abuse under President Macías Nguema.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's 1983 expulsion of illegal immigrants damaged relations with
questions.A: Ghana, whose citizens formed the majority of those expelled
questions.B: Britain, which had to receive the deportees
questions.C: Cameroon, which closed the Bakassi border in protest
questions.D: Libya, which withdrew its ambassador from Lagos
questions.explanation: The expulsion came at a time of economic crisis in both countries.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The principal organ of the United Nations responsible for maintaining international peace and security is the
questions.A: Security Council
questions.B: General Assembly
questions.C: Economic and Social Council
questions.D: International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: The Security Council can impose sanctions and authorise the use of force.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A resolution before the UN Security Council fails when
questions.A: one of the five permanent members votes against it, even if all the others support it
questions.B: fewer than three of the fifteen members of the Council vote in favour of it
questions.C: the General Assembly refuses to approve it by a two-thirds majority of its members
questions.D: the Secretary-General objects to it in writing within seven days of the vote
questions.explanation: The veto belongs to the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China; substantive resolutions also need nine votes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The UN Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994 because
questions.A: the last trust territory, Palau, had become independent
questions.B: it was merged with the Security Council
questions.C: its members failed to pay their dues
questions.D: the General Assembly abolished it
questions.explanation: With all trust territories self-governing, the Council had no remaining work.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The International Court of Justice, which sits at The Hague, differs from national courts in that it
questions.A: settles disputes between states and cannot try individuals
questions.B: tries only criminal cases involving heads of state
questions.C: hears appeals from the Supreme Courts of member states
questions.D: can enforce its judgments with its own police force
questions.explanation: Individuals are tried by the separate International Criminal Court; the ICJ's parties are states.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Organisation of African Unity was replaced by the African Union in 2002 mainly because
questions.A: its strict principle of non-interference had stopped it from acting against coups, civil wars and genocide
questions.B: the OAU had achieved all the aims set out in its charter and voted to dissolve itself at its final summit
questions.C: the United Nations Security Council ordered the change after the OAU failed to pay its dues to the UN
questions.D: the OAU headquarters in Addis Ababa had been destroyed in the war between Ethiopia and Eritrea
questions.explanation: The AU's Constitutive Act allows intervention in grave circumstances and rejects unconstitutional changes of government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A key difference between the OAU Charter and the AU Constitutive Act is that the AU
questions.A: may intervene in a member state in grave circumstances such as genocide and war crimes
questions.B: has no headquarters of its own and meets in a different capital city every year
questions.C: admits only French-speaking African states and excludes the former British colonies
questions.D: excludes the North African countries from membership and covers only sub-Saharan Africa
questions.explanation: Article 4(h) of the Constitutive Act gives the AU this right of intervention.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Treaty of Lagos of 1975 establishing ECOWAS was signed by
questions.A: fifteen West African states
questions.B: the five permanent members of the Security Council
questions.C: all the members of the OAU
questions.D: Nigeria and Ghana only
questions.explanation: Cape Verde joined in 1977 and Mauritania withdrew in 2000, leaving fifteen members until the 2025 withdrawals.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of 1979 allows citizens of member states to
questions.A: enter another member state without a visa and stay for up to ninety days
questions.B: vote in the elections of any member state
questions.C: work as civil servants in any member state without a permit
questions.D: claim citizenship of any member state after one year
questions.explanation: The protocol also provides for the rights of residence and establishment in later phases.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Commonwealth differs from the United Nations in that it
questions.A: is a voluntary association of mostly former British territories with no binding charter
questions.B: has a security council in which five permanent members can veto any decision
questions.C: includes every independent state in the world as a member with an equal vote
questions.D: was founded after the Second World War to prevent the outbreak of another world war
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth works by consensus and declarations such as those of Singapore (1971) and Harare (1991).

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Harare Declaration of 1991 committed Commonwealth members to
questions.A: democracy, human rights and the rule of law, with suspension for members that breach them
questions.B: the abolition of the monarchy in all member states and the adoption of republican constitutions
questions.C: the adoption of the pound sterling as a common currency for trade among the member states
questions.D: military cooperation against communist states and the stationing of British troops in Africa
questions.explanation: Nigeria (1995), Pakistan (1999) and Fiji were suspended under the Harare principles.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Mozambique (1995) and Rwanda (2009) were unusual admissions to the Commonwealth because
questions.A: neither had been a British colony
questions.B: both were still ruled by military governments
questions.C: both had earlier been expelled from the organisation
questions.D: both are located outside Africa
questions.explanation: Gabon and Togo, former French colonies, joined in 2022 on the same basis.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960 by
questions.A: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela
questions.B: Nigeria, Libya, Algeria, Gabon and Angola
questions.C: the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China
questions.D: Egypt, Syria, Jordan, Lebanon and Iraq
questions.explanation: The five founders sought to coordinate petroleum policies and stabilise prices; the headquarters moved to Vienna in 1965.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major weakness of the Organisation of African Unity was
questions.A: its lack of enforcement powers and its dependence on members who often failed to pay their dues
questions.B: its refusal to admit any newly independent state until it had held multi-party elections
questions.C: its domination by the former colonial powers, which appointed its secretary-general and staff
questions.D: its location outside the African continent, which made it difficult for members to attend meetings
questions.explanation: The OAU could pass resolutions but could not compel members to obey them.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Pan-African Parliament of the African Union sits in
questions.A: Midrand, South Africa
questions.B: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
questions.C: Abuja, Nigeria
questions.D: Arusha, Tanzania
questions.explanation: The AU Commission is in Addis Ababa and the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights in Arusha.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations is appointed by
questions.A: the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
questions.B: the five permanent members of the Security Council alone
questions.C: the International Court of Justice
questions.D: a direct vote of the citizens of member states
questions.explanation: Any permanent member can veto a candidate before the Assembly votes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Non-Aligned Movement was founded in Belgrade in 1961 to
questions.A: keep newly independent states out of the rival Cold War blocs
questions.B: unite the communist countries of Eastern Europe
questions.C: promote free trade among the Western democracies
questions.D: coordinate the oil policies of producing countries
questions.explanation: Nehru, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno and Nkrumah were its leading founders.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 after
questions.A: ECOWAS imposed sanctions on them following military coups in the three countries
questions.B: ECOWAS moved its headquarters from Abuja to Accra against the wishes of the three countries
questions.C: they were expelled from the community for failing to pay their dues for more than five years
questions.D: they adopted the naira as their common currency and left the CFA franc zone
questions.explanation: The three military-led states formed the Alliance of Sahel States and gave notice of withdrawal in January 2024.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria became the ninety-ninth member of the United Nations in
questions.A: October 1960
questions.B: January 1963
questions.C: May 1975
questions.D: October 1979
questions.explanation: Nigeria was admitted on 7 October 1960, a week after independence.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's first United Nations peace-keeping deployment was to
questions.A: the Congo in 1960
questions.B: Lebanon in 1978
questions.C: Somalia in 1992
questions.D: Liberia in 1990
questions.explanation: Nigerian troops served in the UN operation in the Congo (ONUC) from 1960 to 1964.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Major-General Joseph Garba of Nigeria served in 1989 to 1990 as
questions.A: President of the United Nations General Assembly
questions.B: Secretary-General of the Commonwealth
questions.C: Chairman of the OAU
questions.D: President of the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: Garba, a former foreign minister, presided over the forty-fourth session of the General Assembly.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Chief Emeka Anyaoku served from 1990 to 2000 as
questions.A: Secretary-General of the Commonwealth
questions.B: Secretary-General of the United Nations
questions.C: Executive Secretary of ECOWAS
questions.D: Secretary-General of OPEC
questions.explanation: Anyaoku was the first African to head the Commonwealth Secretariat in London.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria was readmitted to the Commonwealth in 1999 because
questions.A: it had returned to civilian democratic rule under President Obasanjo
questions.B: it had paid all its outstanding dues to the Commonwealth Secretariat
questions.C: it had agreed to host the Commonwealth Games in Abuja in 2003
questions.D: it had withdrawn all its troops from Sierra Leone and Liberia
questions.explanation: The suspension imposed in 1995 was lifted on 29 May 1999, the day of the handover.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria hosted the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in
questions.A: Abuja in December 2003
questions.B: Lagos in January 1977
questions.C: Kaduna in October 1985
questions.D: Port Harcourt in May 1999
questions.explanation: The Abuja meeting was the first CHOGM held in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the formation of ECOWAS, General Gowon worked most closely with
questions.A: President Gnassingbé Eyadéma of Togo
questions.B: President Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana
questions.C: President Léopold Senghor of Senegal
questions.D: President Félix Houphouët-Boigny of Ivory Coast
questions.explanation: The Nigeria-Togo partnership overcame francophone suspicion of a Nigerian-dominated community.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's admission as a full member of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in 1986 was controversial because
questions.A: Christians saw it as a breach of Nigeria's status as a secular state
questions.B: the OIC required members to adopt Arabic as an official language
questions.C: Nigeria had to leave the Commonwealth to join
questions.D: the OIC was at war with the African Union
questions.explanation: The Christian Association of Nigeria protested strongly and the government set up a committee to review the membership.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's claim to a permanent seat on the UN Security Council rests on
questions.A: its population, its peace-keeping record and its leadership role in Africa
questions.B: its possession of nuclear weapons and a large navy in the Gulf of Guinea
questions.C: its status as a former colonial power with territories in West Africa
questions.D: its membership of the Commonwealth and its close relations with Britain
questions.explanation: Nigeria backs the African Union's Ezulwini Consensus, which demands two permanent seats for Africa.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In 2021 Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first African and the first woman to head the
questions.A: World Trade Organization
questions.B: International Monetary Fund
questions.C: United Nations
questions.D: African Development Bank
questions.explanation: She had earlier served twice as Nigeria's Minister of Finance and as a managing director of the World Bank.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Amina J. Mohammed of Nigeria holds the position of
questions.A: Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations
questions.B: President of the African Development Bank
questions.C: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
questions.D: President of the ECOWAS Commission
questions.explanation: She was appointed in 2017 after serving as Nigeria's Minister of Environment.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria was regarded as a 'frontline state' in the struggle against apartheid, although it is far from Southern Africa, because it
questions.A: gave money, training and diplomatic support to the liberation movements
questions.B: shared a common border with South Africa and Namibia in the south
questions.C: sent its army to invade South Africa and overthrow the apartheid regime
questions.D: hosted the embassy of the apartheid government and traded openly with it
questions.explanation: Nigeria chaired the UN Special Committee against Apartheid and funded the Southern Africa Relief Fund.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Two Nigerians who have served as Secretary-General of OPEC are
questions.A: Rilwanu Lukman and Mohammed Barkindo
questions.B: Joseph Garba and Emeka Anyaoku
questions.C: Taslim Elias and Bola Ajibola
questions.D: Ibrahim Gambari and Amina Mohammed
questions.explanation: Lukman served from 1995 to 2000 and Barkindo from 2016 to 2022.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria delayed signing the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement until July 2019 because
questions.A: manufacturers feared that cheap imports would flood the Nigerian market
questions.B: the agreement required Nigeria to leave ECOWAS
questions.C: Nigeria wanted the secretariat to be located in Abuja
questions.D: the National Assembly had rejected the agreement
questions.explanation: President Buhari signed at the AU summit in Niamey after a committee consulted local businesses.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The location of the ECOWAS Commission, Parliament and Court of Justice in Abuja reflects
questions.A: Nigeria's position as the largest contributor to the community's budget and a founding leader
questions.B: the fact that Nigeria is the only English-speaking member of the community
questions.C: the decision of the United Nations to site all West African bodies in Nigeria
questions.D: the absence of suitable buildings in the other capitals of the community
questions.explanation: Nigeria has provided about a third of the ECOWAS budget and most of the troops for its peace-keeping missions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Justice Taslim Olawale Elias of Nigeria served from 1982 to 1985 as
questions.A: President of the International Court of Justice
questions.B: Secretary-General of the United Nations
questions.C: Chief Judge of the ECOWAS Court
questions.D: President of the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
questions.explanation: Elias, a former Chief Justice of Nigeria, was the first African to preside over the World Court.
